title: CoVAMPnet: Comparative Markov State Analysis for Studying Effects of Drug Candidates on Disordered Biomolecules
authors: Marques SM; Kouba P; Legrand A; Sedlar J; Disson L; Planas-Iglesias J; Sanusi Z; Kunka A; Damborsky J; Pajdla T; Prokop Z; Mazurenko S; Sivic J; Bednar D
one_liner_zh: 该文开发CoVAMPnet框架，结合增强采样MD与马尔可夫状态模型及神经网络梯度分析，量化药物候选分子对无序Aβ42肽构象分布和动力学的影响，聚焦无序蛋白-小分子互作机制建模，方法可迁移至无序蛋白PPI研究。
abstract:
ABSTRACT

Computational study of the effect of drug candidates on intrinsically disordered biomolecules is challenging due to their vast and complex conformational space. Here we developed a Comparative Markov State Analysis (CoVAMPnet) framework to quantify changes in the conformational distribution and dynamics of a disordered biomolecule in the presence and absence of small organic drug candidate molecules. First, molecular dynamics trajectories are generated using enhanced sampling, in the presence and absence of small molecule drug candidates, and ensembles of soft Markov state models (MSMs) are learned for each system using unsupervised machine learning. Second, these ensembles of learned MSMs are aligned across different systems based on a solution to an optimal transport problem. Third, the directional importance of inter-residue distances for the assignment to different conformational states is assessed by a discriminative analysis of aggregated neural network gradients. This final step provides interpretability and biophysical context to the learned MSMs. We applied this novel computational framework to assess the effects of ongoing phase 3 therapeutics tramiprosate (TMP) and its metabolite 3-sulfopropanoic acid (SPA) on the disordered Aβ42 peptide involved in Alzheimer’s disease. Based on adaptive sampling molecular dynamics and CoVAMPnet analysis, we observed that both TMP and SPA preserved more structured conformations of Aβ42 by interacting non-specifically with charged residues. SPA impacted Aβ42 more than TMP, protecting α-helices and suppressing the formation of aggregation-prone β-strands. Experimental biophysical analyses showed only mild effects of TMP/SPA on Aβ42, and activity enhancement by the endogenous metabolization of TMP into SPA. Our data suggest that TMP/SPA may also target other biomolecules than Aβ peptides. The CoVAMPnet method is broadly applicable to study the effects of drug candidates on the conformational behavior of intrinsically disordered biomolecules.

abstract_zh:
摘要

对 intrinsically disordered biomolecules（固有无序生物分子）上候选药物影响的计算研究因其庞大且复杂的构象空间而具有挑战性。在此，我们开发了一个 Comparative Markov State Analysis（CoVAMPnet，比较马尔可夫状态分析）框架，以量化在存在和不存在小分子有机候选药物分子时，无序生物分子的构象分布和动态变化。首先，使用增强采样生成分子动力学轨迹，在存在和不存在小分子候选药物的情况下，并通过无监督机器学习为每个系统学习软马尔可夫状态模型（MSMs）的集合。其次，基于最优传输问题的解，将这些学习到的MSMs集合在不同系统间进行对齐。第三，通过聚合神经网络梯度的判别分析，评估残基间距离对不同构象状态分配的方向重要性。这最后一步为学习到的MSMs提供了可解释性和生物物理背景。我们将这一新颖的计算框架应用于评估正在进行的三期治疗药物 tramiprosate（TMP）及其代谢物 3-sulfopropanoic acid（SPA）对涉及阿尔茨海默病的无序 Aβ42 肽的影响。基于自适应采样分子动力学和 CoVAMPnet 分析，我们观察到 TMP 和 SPA 均通过与带电残基的非特异性相互作用，保留了 Aβ42 更有序的构象。SPA 对 Aβ42 的影响大于 TMP，保护了 α-螺旋并抑制了易聚集的 β-折叠的形成。实验生物物理分析显示 TMP/SPA 对 Aβ42 仅有温和影响，且 TMP 内源性代谢为 SPA 增强了活性。我们的数据表明，TMP/SPA 可能还靶向除 Aβ 肽以外的其他生物分子。CoVAMPnet 方法广泛适用于研究候选药物对固有无序生物分子构象行为的影响。
